title: September 2019 Class College Final Exam (Part 3 of 6)
unit: Comprehensive Nursing (Medical-Surgical, Paediatrics, Midwifery, Community Health, Mental Health, Pharmacology, Research, Leadership and Management)

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the September 2019 class College Final Exam paper (Kenya Registered Nursing, sat 18 November 2022, Multiple Choice Questions, Q41 to Q60).

questions.text: Naturally acquired active immunity, is obtained through the process of:
questions.explanation: Recovery from an infection (C) is correct because in naturally acquired active immunity the person's own immune system meets the pathogen during a real infection and makes antibodies and memory cells, which gives long-lasting protection. Vaccination (A) is incorrect because it gives artificially acquired active immunity. Breast feeding (B) is incorrect because the antibodies (especially IgA) passed in breast milk give naturally acquired passive immunity. Administration of antiserum (D) is incorrect because it gives artificially acquired passive immunity, which is immediate but short-lived.

questions.text: B cells are activated by the presence of:
questions.explanation: Antigens (D) is correct because a B cell is activated when its surface receptor binds a specific antigen (usually with help from T helper cells), after which it multiplies and becomes plasma cells that make antibodies and memory B cells. Antibodies (A) is incorrect because they are the products of activated B cells, not the trigger. Interferons (B) is incorrect because they are antiviral cytokines released by infected cells that warn neighbouring cells. Memory cells (C) is incorrect because they are produced after activation and respond faster on re-exposure to the same antigen.

questions.text: A house built with proper ventilation satisfies the ______ criteria:
questions.explanation: Physical (B) is correct because the physical criteria of a healthy house cover protection from weather and the physical environment, including adequate ventilation, lighting, space, a sound floor, walls and roof, and drainage. Biological (A) is incorrect because it covers protection from pests, vectors, rodents and disease-causing organisms, and safe water and sanitation. Hazard free (C) is incorrect because it concerns safety from accidents such as fire, falls and poisoning. Social (D) is incorrect because it covers privacy, security and the suitability of the home for family and community life.

questions.text: The ideal degrees to store vaccines at the health center are between:
questions.explanation: +2 to +8 degrees (A) is correct because in the cold chain, most vaccines (BCG, measles, pentavalent, PCV, IPV and others) are stored in the refrigerator at +2 to +8 degrees Celsius at health facility level. Vaccines that are damaged by freezing (such as pentavalent and tetanus toxoid) must never be frozen, and a shake test is used to check for freeze damage. -4 to 4 degrees (B) is incorrect because it includes sub-zero temperatures that freeze and spoil sensitive vaccines. 0 to -4 degrees (C) is incorrect because it is a freezing range. -10 to -25 degrees (D) is incorrect because it is the freezer range used for oral polio vaccine at national and regional stores, not for routine storage at a health centre.

questions.text: The immunoglobulin that is abundant in a person's bodily secretions such as saliva and tears is:
questions.explanation: IgA (B) is correct because secretory IgA is the main antibody of mucosal secretions (saliva, tears, breast milk, and respiratory and gut secretions), where it prevents pathogens from attaching to the mucosa. IgG (A) is incorrect because it is the most abundant antibody in blood and the only one that crosses the placenta. IgE (C) is incorrect because it is bound to mast cells and is involved in allergy and parasitic infections. IgD (D) is incorrect because it is found mainly on the surface of B cells as a receptor.

questions.text: Vertigo is defined as:
questions.explanation: Subjective feeling of imbalance (A) is the marked answer because vertigo is a false sensation of movement, usually spinning, that the patient feels and reports (a symptom), commonly with nausea, vomiting and nystagmus, and it arises from the vestibular system or its central pathways. Objective sense of imbalance (B) is incorrect because objective findings are signs seen by the examiner, such as nystagmus or an abnormal gait. Round involvement (C) is incorrect because it has no meaning as a definition of vertigo. Ringing noises in the ears (D) is incorrect because it describes tinnitus.

questions.text: In BLS the second link in the adult chain of survival out of hospital is:
questions.explanation: Early CPR (C) is correct because the out-of-hospital adult chain of survival starts with recognition of cardiac arrest and activation of the emergency response, and the second link is early high-quality CPR (compressions of 5 to 6 cm at 100 to 120 per minute), which keeps blood flowing to the brain and heart. Effective advanced life support (A) is incorrect because it comes later, after defibrillation. Rapid defibrillation with an AED (B) is incorrect because it is the third link. Post cardiac arrest care (D) is incorrect because it comes after return of spontaneous circulation.

questions.text: Neutropenia caused by chemotherapy administration is managed by:

options.A: Administration of a granulocyte colony - stimulating factor
options.C: Dietary increase of iron and folate

questions.explanation: Administration of a granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (A) is correct because G-CSF (filgrastim) stimulates the bone marrow to make neutrophils and shortens the period of neutropenia; the nurse also uses protective isolation, hand hygiene, monitors temperature and reports fever at once. Blood transfusion (B) is incorrect because it treats severe anaemia or thrombocytopenia, not low neutrophils. Dietary increase of iron and folate (C) is incorrect because it treats nutritional anaemia and will not correct drug-induced marrow suppression. Discontinue the chemotherapy (D) is incorrect because stopping or delaying treatment is a decision for the oncologist if the counts do not recover, and it is not the standard first management.

questions.text: Factors that influence drug safety in the elderly include:

options.A: Increased GIT motility, reduced liver function
options.B: Higher body fat percentage, reduced kidney function
options.D: Reduced liver function, poor peripheral circulation

questions.explanation: Reduced liver function, poor peripheral circulation (D) is the marked answer because reduced liver blood flow and enzyme activity slow drug metabolism so drugs accumulate, and poor peripheral circulation slows absorption from intramuscular and subcutaneous sites; others include reduced kidney clearance, polypharmacy and altered body composition. Increased GIT motility, reduced liver function (A) is incorrect because gut motility decreases with age. Higher body fat percentage, reduced kidney function (B) lists real age changes (a larger volume of distribution for fat-soluble drugs and lower renal excretion), so this item is contestable, but the key given is D. Drug interactions, increased GIT motility (C) is incorrect because motility is reduced, not increased.

questions.text: To prevent HIV positive patients from Malaria, toxoplasmosis infection they are covered using:
questions.explanation: Cotrimoxazole (A) is correct because cotrimoxazole preventive therapy protects people living with HIV against Pneumocystis pneumonia, toxoplasmosis, malaria and some bacterial infections such as diarrhoeal disease, and is given daily until immune recovery. Isoniazid therapy (B) is incorrect because it is given to prevent tuberculosis. Sulfadoxine pyrimethamine (C) is incorrect because it is used for intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy and must not be combined with cotrimoxazole, since both are antifolates. Acyclovir (D) is incorrect because it is an antiviral for herpes infections.

questions.text: When using analgesic ladder by WHO, a patient with a pain score of 2 should be given:
questions.explanation: Paracetamol (C) is correct because a pain score of 1 to 3 is mild pain, which is step 1 of the WHO analgesic ladder, treated with non-opioid analgesics (paracetamol or NSAIDs), with or without adjuvants. Tramadol (A) is incorrect because it is a weak opioid for step 2 (moderate pain, score 4 to 6). Betapyn (B) is incorrect because it combines paracetamol with codeine (a weak opioid), doxylamine and caffeine, so it is a step 2 product. Carbamazepine (D) is incorrect because it is an adjuvant anticonvulsant used for neuropathic pain, not the first drug for mild pain.

questions.text: Non maleficence in palliative care involves:

options.C: Allowing the patient to make their own decisions
options.D: Permitting the doctor to decide on the treatment for the patient

questions.explanation: Minimizing harm to patients (B) is correct because non-maleficence means 'do no harm': avoiding treatments whose burdens outweigh the benefits, preventing unnecessary pain and suffering, and not giving futile interventions at the end of life. Prescribing placebos for patients (A) is incorrect because it deceives the patient and breaches veracity. Allowing the patient to make their own decisions (C) is incorrect because it is autonomy. Permitting the doctor to decide on the treatment for the patient (D) is incorrect because it is paternalism, which overrides the patient's autonomy.

questions.text: Principles of hospice care state that:

options.B: Home care of the dying is unnecessary
options.C: Death is a normal part of living

questions.explanation: Death is a normal part of living (C) is correct because hospice care affirms life and regards dying as a natural process, so it neither hastens nor postpones death, and it focuses on comfort, pain and symptom control, and psychosocial and spiritual support for the patient and family. Death must not be accepted (A) is incorrect because hospice philosophy accepts death. Home care of the dying is unnecessary (B) is incorrect because home-based care is a key part of hospice and palliative care in Kenya. Pain builds character (D) is incorrect because hospice care aims to relieve pain, not to let patients suffer.

questions.text: Hormone erythropoietin (EPO) is responsible for:

options.B: Stimulating the formation of the platelets
options.C: Stimulating the proliferation of the progenitor cells
options.D: Regulating the activities of cells involved in non-specific defenses

questions.explanation: Stimulating the production of RBC's (A) is correct because erythropoietin is made mainly by the kidneys in response to low oxygen (hypoxia) and acts on red marrow erythroid progenitor cells to increase red cell production; this is why chronic kidney disease causes anaemia. Stimulating the formation of the platelets (B) is incorrect because that is done by thrombopoietin. Stimulating the proliferation of the progenitor cells (C) is incorrect because it describes the general action of colony-stimulating factors and growth factors, whereas EPO acts specifically on red cell precursors. Regulating the activities of cells involved in non-specific defenses (D) is incorrect because it describes cytokines such as interferons and interleukins.

questions.text: The learner has changed their perception of elderly patients. The learning domain involved is:
questions.explanation: Affective (B) is correct because the affective domain deals with attitudes, feelings, values and beliefs, so a change in how the learner views elderly patients is an attitude change. Cognitive (A) is incorrect because it deals with knowledge, understanding and thinking skills. Psychomotor (C) is incorrect because it deals with practical and physical skills. Mental (D) is incorrect because it is not one of the three learning domains in Bloom's taxonomy.

questions.text: Measurable verbs used in assessing learning outcomes include:
questions.explanation: Formulate, state (C) is correct because learning outcomes are written with action verbs that describe observable and measurable performance, such as state, list, formulate, describe, demonstrate and calculate. Know, understand (A) is incorrect because they are vague and cannot be directly observed or measured. Appreciate, realize (B) is incorrect because these are internal states that cannot be measured directly. Value, enjoy (D) is incorrect because they describe feelings, which are not directly observable.

questions.text: The correct sequence of the three steps of change according to Lewin's model for change is:
questions.explanation: Unfreezing, movement and freezing (C) is correct because in Lewin's model the first step is unfreezing (creating readiness by showing why the current way must change), then movement (the change or transition is carried out) and finally refreezing (the new behaviour is stabilised and made routine). Solid, Unfreezing, and freezing (A) is incorrect because 'solid' is not a step of the model. Movement, unfreezing and freezing (B) is incorrect because movement cannot come before unfreezing. Unfreezing, solid and freezing (D) is incorrect because 'solid' is not a step; the middle step is movement.

questions.text: Resources required to deliver quality health care such as nurses, medical records, building are categorized under:
questions.explanation: Structure (C) is correct because in Donabedian's quality model, structure refers to the resources and setting needed to give care, including staff, buildings, equipment, supplies and records. Processes (A) is incorrect because it refers to the activities of care, such as assessment, procedures and documentation. Practice (B) is incorrect because it is not one of the three Donabedian components (structure, process and outcome). Organization (D) is incorrect because it is not a Donabedian category, and outcomes refer to the results of care such as recovery and satisfaction.

questions.text: The leadership theory that states that 'leaders are born not made' is:
questions.explanation: Great man theory (A) is correct because it holds that leadership qualities are inborn, so great leaders are born with traits such as intelligence, charisma and courage, and cannot be created by training. Behavioral theory (B) is incorrect because it says leadership can be learned through observation and training of behaviours. Scientific theory (C) is incorrect because scientific management (Taylor) focuses on efficiency, task analysis and work methods. System theory (D) is incorrect because it views the organisation as interrelated parts working together toward a common goal.

questions.text: The authority to act is best defined as:
questions.explanation: Having legitimate right to act (C) is correct because authority is the formal, legitimate right given by the position or organisation to make decisions and act within a defined role. Having responsibility to direct others (A) is incorrect because responsibility is the obligation to carry out duties, not the right to act. Being accountable to the organization (B) is incorrect because accountability is being answerable for the results of one's actions. Telling others what to do (D) is incorrect because it describes directing or giving orders, which is only one way authority is exercised.
